questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's reservation system:
1. Total reservation in central services cannot exceed 50% (Indra Sawhney, 1992)
2. The 103rd Amendment (2019) introduced 10% EWS reservation (over and above 50%)
3. SC upheld EWS reservation in Janhit Abhiyan case (2022) by 3:2 majority
4. EWS reservation applies to SCs/STs/OBCs whose income is below ₹8 lakh
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — EWS reservation explicitly EXCLUDES SC/ST/OBC (those already covered by existing reservation). It is ONLY for economically weaker sections among UNRESERVED categories (general category poor). Criteria: family income <₹8 lakh/year, agricultural land <5 acres, residential flat <1000 sq ft, residential plot <100/200 sq yards. The exclusion of SC/ST/OBC from EWS was a key constitutional challenge point — SC upheld it (EWS quota is not for those with existing reservation benefit).

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's food fortification programme:
1. Rice fortification involves adding iron, folic acid, and Vitamin B12
2. It targets anaemia and micronutrient deficiency among the poor
3. Fortified rice is distributed through PDS, Mid-Day Meal, and ICDS
4. India has achieved 100% fortified rice distribution across all states
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — 100% coverage NOT achieved across all states. Phased implementation: started with 'aspirational districts' → expanded gradually. Some states/districts still receiving normal (unfortified) rice. Fortification: Fortified Rice Kernels (FRK) blended with normal rice (1:100 ratio). FSSAI standards mandate: Iron (28-42.5mg/kg), Folic Acid (75-125μg/kg), B12 (0.75-1.25μg/kg). India's anaemia: 57% women (15-49), 67% children (6-59 months) are anaemic — massive public health crisis driving this programme.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about Domestic Violence in India:
1. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) was enacted in 2005
2. It covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, AND economic abuse
3. It provides the right to reside in the 'shared household'
4. Only married women can file complaints under this Act
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — PWDVA is NOT limited to married women. It covers: wives, live-in partners, sisters, mothers, widows — any woman in a 'domestic relationship'. This was a deliberate expansion beyond matrimonial laws. Key provisions: Protection Orders, Residence Orders, monetary relief, custody orders. Domestic violence includes: physical (beating), sexual (marital rape debate — not criminalized separately), verbal (insults, humiliation), emotional (isolation), economic (denial of resources/maintenance). Magistrate can pass ex-parte interim orders.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's Scheduled Tribes and their rights:
1. STs constitute approximately 8.6% of India's population (Census 2011)
2. Fifth Schedule applies to tribal areas in 10 states
3. Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in 4 NE states (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram)
4. PESA (1996) extends Panchayat provisions to all areas of India uniformly
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — PESA does NOT apply uniformly to all areas. It specifically extends Panchayat provisions to SCHEDULED AREAS (Fifth Schedule areas) — not all of India. Non-scheduled areas follow normal 73rd Amendment panchayats. PESA gives Gram Sabhas in scheduled areas special powers over: minor minerals, minor water bodies, village markets, money lending control, intoxicants regulation, land alienation prevention. Fifth Schedule: 10 states (AP, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Odisha, HP).

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's housing crisis:
1. India's urban housing shortage is estimated at 10-12 million units
2. PMAY-Urban aims for 'Housing for All' with interest subsidy on home loans
3. Affordable housing is defined as units costing less than ₹45 lakh in metros
4. Slum population in India is approximately 65 million (Census 2011)
questions.explanation: All correct. Urban housing shortage: estimated 10-12 million units (mainly EWS/LIG categories). PMAY-U: 4 verticals — In-situ Slum Redevelopment, Credit Linked Subsidy (CLSS: ₹2.67 lakh subsidy for EWS/LIG home loans), Affordable Housing in Partnership, Beneficiary-led Construction. Affordable housing: ₹45 lakh cap in metros, ₹30 lakh in non-metros (for CLSS). Slum population: 65.5 million in 2,613 cities/towns (Census 2011, likely 80+ million now). Key challenge: land prices, FSI restrictions, approval delays, construction cost inflation.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to the Right to Food in India:
1. SC in PUCL vs Union of India (2001) recognized Right to Food under Article 21
2. National Food Security Act (2013) provides legal entitlement to food
3. India ranks poorly on the Global Hunger Index
4. India has eliminated all forms of malnutrition through government programmes
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India has NOT eliminated malnutrition. NFHS-5: 35.5% children stunted, 19.3% wasted, 32.1% underweight; 57% women anaemic. India on GHI 2023: ranked 111/125 (category: 'Serious'). India disputed GHI methodology but numbers remain concerning. PUCL case (2001): SC issued continuous orders on food schemes (MDM, ICDS, PDS). NFSA 2013: legal entitlement (5kg/person/month at ₹1-3). Paradox: India is food-surplus (record production) yet food-insecure for millions (access/distribution problem, not production).

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about bonded labour in India:
1. Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was enacted in 1976
2. Bonded labour is prohibited under Article 23 of the Constitution
3. India has completely eradicated bonded labour
4. Brick kilns, stone quarries, and agriculture are sectors with highest prevalence
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG — bonded labour has NOT been completely eradicated. Despite being constitutionally prohibited (Article 23: prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour) and legally abolished (1976 Act), it persists due to: poverty, illiteracy, caste-based exploitation, weak enforcement. Estimated: 18-20 million bonded labourers (ILO/various estimates). Sectors: brick kilns (Punjab, UP), stone quarries (Rajasthan), agriculture (debt bondage), domestic work, beedi rolling. Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourers: ₹1-3 lakh per rescued person.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's Uniform Civil Code (UCC) debate and personal laws:
1. Hindu personal law was reformed by Hindu Code Bills (1955-56)
2. Muslim personal law remains largely uncodified (except some reforms)
3. Triple Talaq was criminalized by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
4. Goa has a common civil code applicable to all religions (Portuguese Civil Code)
questions.explanation: All correct. Hindu Code Bills (Nehru era): Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Hindu Succession Act 1956, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act — reformed Hindu law significantly (widow inheritance, divorce, monogamy). Muslim law: Shariat Application Act 1937 (general), but no comprehensive codification (succession, maintenance still under old Islamic jurisprudence — some reforms via courts). Triple Talaq (Shayara Bano, 2017 — SC struck down instant talaq; criminalised 2019). Goa: Portuguese Civil Code (1867) still applies — common family law for all religions (only state with UCC-like system).
